newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS UPSET VIKINGS, JAGUARS WIN "EXPANSION BOWL".
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS UPSET VIKINGS, JAGUARS WIN "EXPANSION BOWL".

text.p: Brad Daluiso kicked three field goals, Aaron Pierce scored on a reverse and the New York Giants kept Minnesota's offence out of the end zone in handing the Vikings their first loss of the season, 15-10 on Sunday.
"It's a great win for us," said coach Dan Reeves, whose Giants have won two in a row after losing their first three. "Guys were really excited because we know we beat a good football team today."
"The Giants definitely outplayed us," said Vikings coach Dennis Green.

The Vikings, who scored 90 points in their first four games, got their only points on a 69-yard punt return by David Palmer in the second quarter and a 28-yard field goal by Scott Sisson in the fourth.

New York (2-3) took the lead for good when Pierce, the H-back, scored on a one-yard run off a reverse with 2:53 left in the third quarter after the Giants converted a fourth-down play. It was their first rushing touchdown of the year.

Minnesota held a 7-6 lead when Jason Sehorn knocked the ball away from Vikings quarterback Warren Moon on a corner blitz and defensive end Chad Bratzke recovered the fumble at the Minnesota 49-yard line, setting up the go-ahead TD.
An interception by Giants cornerback Phillippi Sparks at the New York three-yard line with four minutes left preserved the win.

Dave Brown completed 18-of-29 passes for 167 yards and Rodney Hampton ran for a season-high 82 yards on 24 carries for New York. Moon completed 13-of-25 passes for just 143 yards and Robert Smith rushed for 86 yards on 17 carries.

In Jacksonville, the Jaguars rushed for a season-high 179 yards, including a pair of touchdowns by James Stewart, and defeated the Carolina Panthers 24-14 in the first regular-season meeting of last year's expansion teams.
"We earned it and proved something to ourselves," said Jacksonville coach Tom Coughlin.
The Panthers (3-1) entered the game unbeaten and in sole possession of first-place in the NFC West, but fell in the so-called "Expansion Bowl."
"If they feel like this is their Super Bowl so be it," said Carolina linebacker Lamar Lathon.

In San Diego, John Carney's fifth field goal of the game -- a 33-yarder with 3:17 remaining -- lifted the Chargers to a 22-19 victory over the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs in a key AFC West showdown.
Linebacker Junior Seau set up Carney's game-winner when he intercepted a 3rd-and-9 pass by Steve Bono.
Kansas City's Pete Stoyanovich, who already had made four field goals, had a potential game-tying 47-yarder blocked by defensive end Chris Mims.

In San Francisco, Jeff Wilkins tied a club record with six field goals and Elvis Grbac filled in for the injured Steve Young and passed for 222 yards and a touchdown as the 49ers routed the Atlanta Falcons 39-17.

Bobby Hebert, named as the starter by Falcons coach June Jones after Jeff George was suspended for disciplinary reasons, was intercepted three times. Hebert completed 17-of-32 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns.
In Seattle, Brett Favre threw four touchdown passes -- two to Antonio Freeman -- and the Green Bay Packers took advantage of five turnovers to pummel the Seahawks 31-10.
Favre leads the league with 16 touchdown passes.

In Chicago, Jeff Jaeger, in his second game with the Bears, burned the team that cut him with four field goals including a a 30-yarder with 11 seconds left for a 19-17 victory over the Oakland Raiders.
"It's a little ironic they gave up on me and it feels good to come back," said Jaeger. "It was a great game to have against the Raiders."
In Cincinnati, John Elway threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns to lead the Denver Broncos past the Bengals, 14-10.
Broncos running back Terrell Davis gained 112 yards on 24 carries for his fourth straight 100-yard rushing performance.

In Pittsburgh, Mike Tomczak threw two touchdowns in the first eight minutes and Jerome Bettis ran for 115 yards as the Steelers took a 30-16 victory over the Houston Oilers in an AFC Central Division battle.
The Oilers committed five turnovers that led to 17 Pittsburgh points.

At Arizona, LeShon Johnson rambled 66 yards on the second play of overtime, setting up Greg Davis's 24-yard field goal at 1:54 as the Cardinals rallied for the final 17 points in a 31-28 victory over the St Louis Rams.

In Baltimore, Ernest Byner ran for 149 yards and Vinny Testaverde threw a pair of touchdown passes, including the go-ahead score to Michael Jackson early in the fourth quarter, as the Ravens beat the winless New Orleans Saints 17-10.
New Orleans has started the season with five straight defeats for the second straight year.

At Tampa Bay, Bennie Blades scored on a 98-yard interception return late in the first quarter and Scott Mitchell threw for a pair of touchdowns as the Detroit Lions routed the winless Buccaneers 27-0.
In the night game, Leslie Shpeherd and Terry Allen each scored two touchdowns as the Washington Redskins kept the New York Jets winless with a 31-16 victory.
Washington (4-1) has won four straight, its longest streak since winning 11 in a row to start the 1991 season. The Jets (0-5) are off to their worst start since opening the 1980 campaign 0-5.

Trailing 24-16 midway through the fourth quarter, New York had an apparent touchdown pass to Keyshawn Johnson first ruled offensive interference and then an interception by cornerback Tom Carter, who stripped Johnson as he came down with the ball.
